matchstick.title: Compute numeric values and discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Before moving any matchstick, compute the integer values of both sides of the equation and determine the numeric discrepancy; this tells you how much the left side must increase or decrease to match the right side.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after reading the equation, as the first step of the solution.
matchstick.example: Skipping the computation and moving a stick arbitrarily, which often leaves the equation still unbalanced.

matchstick.title: List possible single‑stick transformations
matchstick.principle: Enumerate every way a single matchstick can be moved to turn a Roman numeral or operator into another valid symbol, considering both removal from one character and addition to another.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Right after the discrepancy is known, to generate the pool of candidate moves.
matchstick.example: Failing to list the transformation that turns a '+' into a '-' by removing its vertical stick, thereby missing a viable solution.

matchstick.title: Match numeric difference to value change of a single‑stick move
matchstick.principle: Select a stick move whose effect on the numeric values (increase or decrease) exactly equals the computed discrepancy, ensuring the equation can balance with one move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After generating possible transformations, compare each transformation’s numeric impact with the required difference.
matchstick.example: Choosing a move that changes a numeral by 2 while the discrepancy is 1, resulting in a still‑incorrect equality.

matchstick.title: Validate resulting characters are legal Roman symbols or operators
matchstick.principle: After applying a candidate stick relocation, verify that every character (both numerals and operators) remains a recognized Roman numeral or an allowed operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after proposing a stick move, before accepting it as a solution.
matchstick.example: Leaving a V with only one diagonal stick, which is not a valid Roman numeral, and thus producing an invalid equation.

matchstick.title: Consider intra‑character stick repositioning
matchstick.principle: Allow a stick to be moved within the same character to change its shape (e.g., reposition a diagonal stick in a V to become an X) without affecting any other character.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When enumerating transformations for each individual character.
matchstick.example: Ignoring the possibility of turning a V into an X by moving one of its sticks, thereby missing a potential solution.

matchstick.title: Explore operator modification via the equals sign
matchstick.principle: Consider taking a horizontal stick from the '=' sign (or adding one) to turn it into a '-' sign (or back into '=') while ensuring the equation still contains a valid equals sign somewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric discrepancy suggests that changing the equality operator could help balance the equation.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal bar from '=', turning it into '-', but forgetting to create a new '=' elsewhere, leaving the equation without an equality sign.

matchstick.title: Explore operator modification via the plus sign
matchstick.principle: Consider moving the vertical stick of a '+' sign to turn it into a '-' sign (or adding a vertical stick to a '-' to make '+'), and optionally relocate that stick to another character to adjust its value.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy can be resolved by changing the operation, or when a stick from the '+' can be useful elsewhere.
matchstick.example: Changing '+' to '-' but not placing the removed vertical stick onto another numeral, resulting in an invalid character.

matchstick.title: Consider inter‑character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: When moving a matchstick, allow it to be taken from one character (numeral or operator) and placed onto a different character, thereby changing both characters' shapes; this expands the set of possible single‑stick moves beyond intra‑character changes.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After listing intra‑character transformations, also examine moves that transfer a stick between distinct characters, especially between operators and numerals, to adjust values on both sides of the equation.
matchstick.example: Assuming a stick can only be moved within the same character, missing the solution where a stick from the '+' sign is moved to the left‑hand numeral to turn ‘II = XIV + XI’ into ‘III = XIV – XI’.
